metaData.originalTitle: Introducing the Recommended Agent in AI Chat with Codex as the current choice
metaData.title: Introducing the Recommended Agent in AI Chat with Codex as the current choice
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: JetBrains announces Codex as the recommended default agent in JetBrains AI, based on systematic evaluation across real-world coding benchmarks and online A/B testing.
metaData.summary: This post explains how JetBrains selected Codex (powered by OpenAI) as the recommended coding agent in JetBrains AI. The evaluation used a benchmark dataset of real software engineering tasks across Java, C#, and Python, measuring solve rate, cost, and latency. After comparing candidates (including Junie with Gemini models), Codex with GPT-5.4-mini medium reasoning emerged as the top performer in both offline benchmarks and online A/B tests. The article details the methodology, including cost constraints (avoiding more than 2% of users exceeding $20/month), and provides transparent data via the DPAIA repository. It also emphasizes that users can still switch agents freely.

mainPoints.point: Codex was selected as the recommended agent based on a systematic evaluation across three ecosystem benchmarks.
mainPoints.explanation: The evaluation used 225 Java, 38 C#, and 90 Python tasks from real codebases, measuring solve rate, cost, and latency. Codex with GPT-5.4-mini medium reasoning achieved the best overall balance.

mainPoints.point: Cost constraints were applied early: setups that would push more than 2% of users over $20/month were ruled out before ranking on quality and latency.
mainPoints.explanation: This ensures the recommendation is practical for typical users, not just the most powerful model.

mainPoints.point: The offline benchmark was validated with an online A/B test tracking real user behavior (engagement, agent switching, failure rate).
mainPoints.explanation: Codex outperformed Junie in the A/B test, which tipped the decision despite close offline results.

mainPoints.point: The recommendation is not permanent; JetBrains will re-evaluate as models evolve, agents join, and benchmark coverage grows.
mainPoints.explanation: This highlights a commitment to data-driven iteration rather than a fixed choice.

keyQuotes: JetBrains evaluated coding agents on the things that matter in practice: can they solve real software engineering tasks, quickly and at a cost that makes sense.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces workspace agents, a new class of shared, long-running AI agents within ChatGPT for business teams, designed to automate complex workflows, integrate with organizational tools, and operate under enterprise-grade controls.

relatedArticles.title: The Road to Responsive IntelliJ-Based IDEs
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details JetBrains' multi-year, ongoing effort to improve UI responsiveness in IntelliJ-based IDEs by moving performance-critical write actions off the UI thread, tackling deep architectural constraints in the 25-year-old platform.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.7
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, a significant upgrade over Opus 4.6 with major improvements in advanced software engineering, vision capabilities, instruction following, and autonomous long-horizon reasoning, while implementing new cyber safeguards and maintaining the same pricing.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.

relatedArticles.title: What’s New in PyCharm 2026.1
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: PyCharm 2026.1 introduces a new debugpy-based debugging engine, uv remote interpreter support, expanded free web development tools, and enhanced AI capabilities including an Agent Registry and predictive Next Edit Suggestions.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: The Dev Containers Story: Introducing EelApi for Plugin Authors
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces EelApi, a new IntelliJ Platform API for plugin authors to handle execution environments like local machine, WSL, Docker, and Dev Containers, with code examples and best practices.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding AI's Impact on Developer Workflows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A two-year mixed-methods study by JetBrains HAX team reveals that AI coding assistants subtly reshape developer workflows in ways often misaligned with developers' own perceptions, increasing code output and editing activity while not reducing context switching.

relatedArticles.title: From Java to Wayland: A Pixel’s Journey
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep technical dive into the Java 2D graphics pipeline, explaining how Java applications render pixels and interface with the Wayland windowing system on Linux.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.
